title: Give every pool thread a name and a deliberate daemon status

blocks.text: The billing service has a dozen thread pools, all created with `Executors`' default factory. Two things went wrong last month. During an incident, on-call took a thread dump and found 37 threads called `pool-<N>-thread-<M>`, and had to guess which pool belonged to which component. And after a routine restart, the audit log was missing its last entries: the audit pool is created lazily, on the first audit event, and that event is raised by the housekeeping thread, which is a daemon.

The team now creates every pool with a `ServiceThreads` factory, which knows the component's name and whether the component is background work that may be dropped at exit (a CPU sampler) or foreground work that must finish (audit, ledger). Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/ServiceThreads.java`:

items: `newThread(...)`: the thread a pool asks for.

blocks.text: When you're done, a thread dump shows `audit-1`, `audit-2`, `ledger-1`, ... (each component counting its own threads), and whether the JVM waits for a pool's threads at exit depends only on what the component declared, whichever thread happened to create the pool. About four lines in total.
The tests build real pools with the factory and also call it from a daemon thread.

cases.says: a pool built with the factory runs its tasks on threads named after the component, daemon exactly when the component is background, and the factory hands back its threads unstarted
each factory numbers its own threads from 1, whatever other factories have created
a foreground component's threads are non-daemon even when the factory is called from a daemon thread

origin.section: A Daemon Thread Doesn't Hold the JVM Open, and Exit Drops It Mid-Step

concepts: A platform thread not told otherwise inherits the daemon status of the thread that creates it, so code that creates threads for work that must finish sets daemon status explicitly.
Threads are named where they are created, by the constructor, a builder's counter or a ThreadFactory; generated names and unnamed virtual threads make thread dumps unreadable.
